description: Allow-list of the brand residue gate (scripts/verify-sylvode-brand-residue.sh, ADR-0020 判据 4). Each entry covers the hits of its pattern in the files its paths match, within one repository; anything else named OpenPR/openpr is a failure. Reason codes: stable_identifier, legacy_alias_documented, formerly_note, migration_page, redirect_rule, historical_document, frozen_evidence, legacy_behaviour_test, kept_repository_url.

entries.explanation: Schema and version identifiers carried in API payloads, receipts, cursors and gate files (openpr.form.schema.v1, openpr.event.v1, openpr.plugin.v1, ...). ADR-0020 D3 keeps REST /api/v1 and its schema identifiers unchanged with no removal planned.

JSON Schema $id URLs and the schema file names they resolve to; the v0.9 matrix (testing/fixtures/v09-openpr-schema-ids.json) freezes them and D3 keeps schema identifiers. Also covers the tracked file names that carry the identifier.

The WASM plugin ABI exports and WIT package/world names; ADR-0020 D3 lists the plugin ABI (openpr_alloc, openpr_invoke, openpr_plugin_abi_version, openpr-plugin-v1.wit) as not renamed. Also covers the tracked file names that carry the identifier.
Legacy X-OpenPR-MCP-* attribution and X-OpenPR-Attachment-* count headers, sent and accepted next to the X-Sylvode-* spelling throughout 1.x (ADR-0020 D3; CHANGELOG Deprecated table).
The compatibility token kept in the outbound webhook User-Agent comment section (`Sylvode-Webhook/1.0 (compatible; OpenPR-Webhook/1.0)`), required by ADR-0020 D3.
The legacy config/openpr.toml and config/openpr.compose*.toml names, still discovered with a deprecation warning until v2.0 (ADR-0020 D1/D2), and the documentation and tests that name them.
The openpr:// MCP resource URI alias, still answered with _meta.deprecation until v2.0 (ADR-0020 D1/D2).

The openpr-<target> and openpr-frontend.tar.gz release archive aliases published next to the sylvode-* archives (ADR-0020 D1), and the removed openpr-mcp-server-<target> archives in the release notes.

entries.pattern: postgres(?:ql)?://[^\s\"'`]*openpr[^\s\"'`]*|-U openpr(?: -d (?:openpr|postgres))?|-d openpr|pg_dump -U openpr openpr|POSTGRES_(?:DB|USER|PASSWORD)[:=] ?openpr\w*|(?:DROP|CREATE) DATABASE (?:IF EXISTS )?openpr|openpr_backup_|openpr_dev_password|DATABASE_URL=postgres://openpr[^\s\"]*|\$\{POSTGRES_PORT\}/openpr|PG(?:DATABASE|USER):-openpr
entries.explanation: Database, role and backup names: ADR-0020 D3 keeps database names, roles, tables, columns and the migration history. Backup files keep the openpr_backup_ prefix so existing backups stay in rotation and listing, and development databases created by scripts/dev-up.sh keep their openpr_dev_password; both are listed under "Not renamed" in docs/sylvode-v1.0-compatibility.md.
The compose network name, kept with the compose service labels by ADR-0020 D3.
PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY channel names shared by every API process of a deployment; a rename would split a rolling upgrade, so they are database-level identifiers kept under D3.

Synthetic identities stored in the users table: the bot user domain (`<id>@bot.openpr.local`, any local part, as the API and the gate fixtures create them), the bot JWT subject email (`bot+{}@openpr.local`) and the built-in admin seeded by migration 0008 (`admin@openpr.local`). Existing rows carry these values; D3 keeps database data unchanged.

The governed skill key `openpr-mcp`: served as the MCP resource sylvode://skills/openpr-mcp, stored in scenario templates by migration 0029, and the path of the skill package. Renaming it is a resource-URI change that needs its own compatibility alias. Also covers the tracked file names that carry the identifier.
The Sylvode Webhook repository keeps its URL github.com/openprx/openpr-webhook (ADR-0020 D4 renames only the main repository).
The legacy Sylvode Webhook executable and image names (openpr-webhook, ghcr.io/openprx/openpr-webhook, /app/openpr-webhook) kept through 1.x by ADR-0020 D4.
The browser localStorage key under which users' saved import column mappings live; renaming it silently discards every saved mapping.
The integration provider value the built-in scenario templates store (migration 0029); the smoke asserts what the API returns.
Applied migrations are immutable history (ADR-0020 D3: database names and the migration history are not renamed).
File names of the signed 2026-05-31 Universal Forms acceptance bundle; its manifest, checksums and the report generators identify the bundle by these names.

The frozen v0.9 compatibility matrix fixture and gate keys (testing/fixtures/v09-openpr-schema-ids.json, the v0.9 rc compose project, the v0.9 gate check ids). Also covers the tracked file names that carry the identifier.
The repository path pinned as a const in the frozen v0.3/v0.4 gate receipt schemas, and the producer and exemption that must match it.
Compatibility matrices and the upgrade guide: they exist to name every OpenPR-era identifier next to its replacement.
Release history: releases up to 0.2.21 were published as OpenPR, and the rename entries name the legacy identifiers they deprecate.
Dated plan and audit records of the OpenPR era (container names, commands as run then); kept as written, not current instructions.
Frozen Flow engine and legacy-pages spikes with their recorded evidence (bundle metafiles, environment topology, inventories), captured under the OpenPR name.

entries.pattern: \(formerly OpenPR(?: Webhook)?;?\)?|Formerly OpenPR\.|published as OpenPR|OpenPR-era|Legacy OpenPR names|legacy OpenPR filenames|OpenPR names \(|OpenPR compatibility names
entries.explanation: Notes that Sylvode was formerly OpenPR and that OpenPR-era names keep working (ADR-0020 D4: documentation keeps the 'formerly OpenPR' note).
Tests and gates whose subject is the legacy behaviour: legacy config discovery, the deprecation notices, the URI aliases, the v0.9 rename matrix and the install/upgrade path from OpenPR releases.

The retained legacy configuration example for deployments that keep config/openpr.toml (ADR-0020 D1); it describes the legacy path as such. Also covers the tracked file names that carry the identifier.
Tests that the openpr:// alias and the legacy configuration name keep working.
Static checks that forbid OpenPR-era container aliases, a machine path and the old default database password from returning.
The brand residue gate itself: its pattern, probes, mutation controls and allow-list must spell out the names they look for.
CONTRIBUTING's description of the brand residue gate names the strings it searches for.
The release form of the gate names the webhook checkout by its kept repository name (ADR-0020 D4).
The v1.0 gate chain and its runbook name the webhook checkout, and its residue-scan name, by the kept repository name (ADR-0020 D4).
A hard gate key the v1.0 gate contract defines (gates/v1.0-gate.yaml); the chain must spell it exactly as the contract does.
The webhook repository keeps the URL github.com/openprx/openpr-webhook (ADR-0020 D4), including its README anchors.

entries.pattern: [Ff]ormerly (?:`OpenPR`|OpenPR) Webhook|called OpenPR Webhook|Migrating from OpenPR Webhook|from OpenPR Webhook|Display name OpenPR Webhook
entries.explanation: Notes that Sylvode Webhook was formerly OpenPR Webhook (ADR-0020 D4).

Legacy executable, image, archive, service, launch agent, log target and signature/attribution header names kept through 1.x by ADR-0020 D4, with the code that resolves them. Limited to the files that carry the compatibility layer or document it: packaging, the compat module, the signature and attribution code, their tests, and the release notes.
The event envelope version the Sylvode API sends (events-v1 schema identifier, D3).
Test cases of the legacy x-openpr-signature header.
Cloudflare Pages redirects from the old /openpr and /openpr-webhook paths (ADR-0020 D4: old documentation paths must redirect, not 404).
The migration guide in every locale; it exists to list the OpenPR names and their replacements.
Links to the migration guide page (its slug names the old product).
Link texts and sidebar entries that point at the migration guide ('Migrating from OpenPR').
'Sylvode was formerly named OpenPR' notes (ADR-0020 D4).
The webhook repository URL is kept (ADR-0020 D4).
The compatibility token in the outbound webhook User-Agent (ADR-0020 D3).
Legacy X-OpenPR-* headers documented as accepted or sent through 1.x (ADR-0020 D3/D4).
Legacy config files and openpr:// URIs, still accepted with deprecation warnings until v2.0 (ADR-0020 D1/D2).
Legacy Sylvode Webhook executable, image, archive, service and log-target names kept through 1.x (ADR-0020 D4).

entries.pattern: postgres(?:ql)?://[^\s\"'`]*openpr[^\s\"'`]*|-U openpr(?: -d openpr)?|-d openpr|POSTGRES_(?:DB|USER): openpr|role `openpr`|`openpr` database|database and role `openpr`|named `openpr`|openpr_backup_|openpr-network
entries.explanation: Database, role, backup and compose network names kept by ADR-0020 D3.
The skill key openpr-mcp served as sylvode://skills/openpr-mcp (see the matching sylvode entry).
The opening note of the Sylvode index page in every locale says the product was formerly OpenPR.
The upgrade section points releases published under the OpenPR name at the migration guide.
The database and role name `openpr` in the installation and backup instructions (ADR-0020 D3).
The related-repositories table names the webhook repository by its kept name and URL (ADR-0020 D4).
Redirects from the old /openpr product pages to /sylvode (ADR-0020 D4).

entries.pattern: formerly (?:named )?OpenPR|Formerly OpenPR|原名 OpenPR|ადრე OpenPR|ყოფილი სახელი: OpenPR|Прежнее название — OpenPR|when OpenPR was renamed Sylvode|OpenPR 更名为 Sylvode|OpenPR-ის Sylvode-ად
entries.explanation: 'Formerly OpenPR' notes in every locale (ADR-0020 D4).
The webhook repository URL and checkout directory are kept (ADR-0020 D4).
The legacy Sylvode Webhook executable and image names kept through 1.x (ADR-0020 D4).
The compatibility token in the outbound webhook User-Agent (ADR-0020 D3).
The organisation profile notes that Sylvode was formerly OpenPR (ADR-0020 D4).
The webhook repository keeps its URL (ADR-0020 D4).
The database URL every database test reads; CI and developer environments set it. Listed under "Not renamed" in docs/sylvode-v1.0-compatibility.md.
Legacy compose variables that scripts/start.sh still reads with a deprecation warning (ADR-0020 D2), as listed in the compose row of the v1.0 compatibility matrix.

Environment inputs of the gate scripts, smokes, test suites and build (for example OPENPR_V10_CAPACITY_RESULT, OPENPR_FRONTEND_URL, OPENPR_BUILD_GIT_COMMIT): CI jobs, release builds and frozen gate runs set them by these names, so renaming one needs an alias. Listed under "Not renamed" in docs/sylvode-v1.0-compatibility.md.

Rust type names of the internal API client and configuration (OpenPrClient, OpenPrConfig); not visible to users, renamed only with a refactor that touches every caller. Two scripts name OpenPrConfig::load when they check or describe the Rust source.
The legacy safe-mode environment variable, still read with a deprecation notice (ADR-0020 D2), the code and tests that resolve it, and the release notes that describe it.
An environment entry in the dispatcher's test configurations, passed through to an agent unchanged; the test checks pass-through, not the name.
Legacy environment variables that scripts/start.sh, the demo bootstrap and Sylvode Webhook still read with a deprecation notice (ADR-0020 D2), named where the pages document them.
